abstract: Animal and fungal cells divide through the assembly of a contractile acto-myosin ring (CR) tightly associated with the plasma membrane (PM). To accommodate the CR, extensive remodeling of the PM and the cortical ER (cER) is required. These events allow the recruitment of the anillin Mid1 to the division site in fission yeast, which is defective in pdk1Δ mutants. To identify the mechanism underlying Pdk1 contribution to cytokinesis, we performed a phospho-proteomics analysis of the pdk1Δ mutant, which allowed the identification of the N terminus of the eisosome component Pil1 as a major Pdk1 target. Pil1 N terminus contributes to Pil1 interaction with other Pil1 molecules for high-order molecular structure formation. Defective control of Pil1 by Pdk1 results in the inability to disassemble eisosomes from the division region. Additionally, the absence of Pdk1 impairs the targeting of cER remodelers to the division zone, compromising the tubulation of the cER. Regulation of both processes by Pdk1 ensures successful division plane positioning.
